title: Regional trace-forwarder: lightweight bridge for per-region exporter selection and tenant-aware throttling
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Background:
Redwood's hosted and dedicated customers operate across multiple regions and sometimes require region-local trace export for compliance, latency, or cost reasons. Current tracing ingest funnels traces into a single central exporter pipeline which causes added cross-region egress, brittle failover behavior, and difficulty enforcing tenant-level export quotas.

Goal:
Build a lightweight, region-aware trace-forwarder (a small stateful bridge) that sits near ingest and routes/forwards trace batches to the appropriate backend exporter per-tenant and per-region policy. The forwarder should support dynamic exporter selection, tenant-aware throttling, header normalization, and a graceful fallback to central exporters on failure.

Non-goals:
- Not a full replacement for the runtime exporter stack; this is a routing/forwarding shim focused on selection and throttling.
- Not implementing new storage backends or long-term retention; destination exporters remain responsible for storage.

Acceptance criteria:
- Forwarder can route traces to one of multiple configured exporter endpoints based on tenant and region mapping rules.
- Implements token-bucket throttling per tenant and per exporter (configurable rates).
- Preserves trace context (traceid/spanid/traceflags) and propagation headers across forwarding.
- Emits Prometheus-ready metrics for forwarded/failed/dropped spans and current throttle utilization.
- Supports configuration refresh without restart and logs configuration changes to audit log.
- Fallback path: if regional exporter is unavailable, buffered batches are retried with exponential backoff and if retry budget exhausted, batches are forwarded to central exporter with a distinguishable tag.

Design highlights:
- Stateless control, small local cache: use a compact in-memory routing table (LRU with TTL) keyed by tenant ID -> exporter endpoint(s) populated from central control plane.
- Throttling: local token buckets per tenant and per exporter endpoint. Global guardrail configured per-region to avoid blast radius.
- Payload handling: implement simple payload slicing to keep forwarded batch sizes under 64KB (configurable) and attach forwarding metadata header X-RW-Forwarded: <region,policy,attempt>.
- Observability: forwarder exposes /metrics, /healthz, and /debug/queue endpoints; spans that are dropped include a log line with tenant and reason and an event metric.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Spec and config schema (Confluence) - include policy language for mapping tenant->exporter and priority fallback rules.
2) Prototype in Go using existing OTLP client libraries; unit tests for token buckets, routing decisions, header preservation.
3) Integrate with control-plane config push (k8s ConfigMap watcher + central config API fallback).
4) Add Prometheus metrics and dashboard panels for forwarded/dropped rates and per-tenant throttle heatmap.
5) Canary deploy to staging region; collect workload traces and validate latency/regression.
6) Rollout with feature flags to limit enabled tenants initially.

Tasks (candidate checklist):
- [ ] Finalize Confluence design doc and policy DSL (owner: Aisha) (link below).
- [ ] Implement routing table and config watcher (owner: Liam).
- [ ] Implement token-bucket throttle + tests (owner: Sanjay Patel).
- [ ] Forwarder binary with OTLP HTTP/gRPC client adapters (owner: Priya Nair).
- [ ] Metrics (Prometheus) and dashboard skeleton (owner: Observability UX).
- [ ] Add e2e test harness that injects exporter failures and measures fallback behavior (owner: QA).

Tradeoffs and notes:
- Keeping the forwarder lightweight favors in-memory routing and simple token buckets; this reduces operational complexity but requires careful handling of stale config. TTL and versioned config pushes mitigate this.
- We avoid introducing per-tenant persistent queues for now to reduce storage surface; instead, we perform bounded in-memory buffering with retry and eventual fallback to central exporter.
